docs.title: What is MiSAR?
docs.text:
MiSAR is an approach that follows the Model Driven Architecture to semi-automatically generate architectural models of implemented microservice systems.

A video demonstration of MiSAR can be found at:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sdRDkLesyS0

MiSAR consists of a parser that creates a Platform Specific Model from existing systems and a Model Transformation engine that transforms platform Specifc Models into Platform Independent Model instances. An instance of a MiSAR Platform Independent Model is the recovered architectural model of the implemented microservice system.

docs.title: Workflow Overview
docs.text:
1. Parse code → Generate PSM (Platform Specific Model)
  2. Transform PSM → PIM (Platform Independent Model)
  3. Generate UML diagrams (optional)

docs.title: Create PIM (Platform Independent Model)
docs.text: In this part, you will learn how to transform a generated PSM instance into a PIM instance using the MiSAR QVT transformation.

docs.title: Important
docs.text:
Before running the transformation, ensure that the PSM file generated by the parser is imported into the Eclipse project.

You can simply copy the generated PSM file into the Eclipse project directory.

This PSM file must be selected as the source model during transformation.

docs.title: Open Transformation
docs.text: Right click: MisarTransformation3.qvto → Run As → Run Configurations

docs.title: Select Transformation
docs.text: Choose: QVT Operational Transformation

docs.title: Input (PSM)
docs.text:
Select generated PSM file (.xmi)

NOTE: If the file is not present in the project, it will not appear in the selection list.

docs.title: Output (PIM)
docs.text: Choose output location and filename

docs.title: Run Transformation
docs.text: Click Run

docs.title: View Output
docs.text: Right click generated file → Open With → Sample Reflective Ecore Model Editor

docs.title: Result
docs.text: You will see: - Microservices - Functional vs Infrastructure services - Dependencies

docs.title: Create PSM (Platform Specific Model)
docs.text: In this part, you will learn how to use the MiSAR Parser to generate a Platform Specific Model (PSM) from an existing microservice codebase.

docs.title: Launch Parser
docs.text: Run python3 MiSAR.py to open the MiSAR AIO interface, then click Launch under MiSAR Parser.

docs.title: Fill Required Fields
docs.text:
• Project Name
  • Project Root Directory
  • Output Directory (where PSM will be saved)
  • Module Directories
  • Docker Compose file

docs.title: Automatic Importer (For Docker Compose)
docs.text:
When you add a Docker Compose file, the parser can attempt to auto-populate the remaining required fields.

When prompted, click Yes to auto-detect project files.

docs.title: After Import
docs.text:
The UI will populate: - Docker services - Module paths - POM files

You can manually edit/remove entries.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: If required fields are missing, an error message will appear after clicking Create PSM Model. The missing fields will also be highlighted.

docs.title: Generate PSM
docs.text: Click Create PSM Model

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
If the process completes successfully, the PSM file will be generated in the selected output directory.

Note: Depending on the version, a success message may also be displayed showing the file location.

docs.title: Graphical Model Generator
docs.text: This is the final step in the MiSAR process, where the recovered PIM is transformed into visual representations (UML diagrams) and summaries.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This step is optional and generates UML diagrams.

docs.title: Launch Graphical Model Generator
docs.text: Run python3 MiSAR.py to open MiSAR AIO, then click Launch

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
Provide the PIM file generated from the transformation step.

If you don't have a PIM file, you can simply change the file extension of the generated PIM file from .xmi to .PIM (case-sensitive) and use that as input.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• UML diagrams
  • Excel summaries
  • Architecture overview

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Useful for visualising system structure
  • Helps in analysis and reporting

docs.title: Running MiSAR (First Launch)
docs.text:
To launch the MiSAR All-In-One (AIO) tool:

  1. Open a terminal
  2. Navigate to the MiSAR project directory
  3. Run:
python3 MiSAR.py

When running MiSAR for the first time, it will detect missing dependencies:

Click Yes to install them automatically.

docs.title: After Installation
docs.text: A success message will confirm everything is installed correctly.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Ensure Python 3.11+ is installed
  • Ensure you have an active internet connection for automatic module installation

docs.title: QVT Operational – Manual Installation
docs.text:
You can safely skip this guide if the last step, QVT Configuration, worked without errors, and you can run transformations.

In some Eclipse installations, QVT Operational (QVTo) may not be available by default.

If you do not see:

Run As → QVT Operational Transformation

or QVT-related options in Eclipse, you will need to install QVTo manually.

docs.title: Option 1 – Eclipse Marketplace
docs.text:
You can try installing QVTo via the Eclipse Marketplace:

Go to:

Help → Eclipse Marketplace

Search for:

QVT Operational

Click Install and follow the steps.

In newer Eclipse versions, QVTo may not appear in Marketplace. If it does not show, use the manual installation method below.

docs.title: Option 2 – Install from Eclipse Update Site (Recommended)
docs.text: This method installs QVTo directly from the Eclipse update site. You do not need to download the .zip file manually.

docs.title: Step 1 – Open Install New Software
docs.text:
Open Eclipse.

Go to:

Help → Install New Software...

docs.title: Step 2 – Add the QVTo Update Site
docs.text:
Click Add...

In the Add Repository window, enter:

Name: QVTo 3.11.2 Release Latest
Location: https://download.eclipse.org/mmt/qvto/builds/release/latest/

Click Add.

docs.title: Step 3 – Select Components
docs.text:
After Eclipse loads the available software, select:

  • QVT Operational
  • QVT Operational (tests)

Click:

Next

docs.title: Step 4 – Review Install Details
docs.text:
Review the items to be installed.

You should see QVT Operational components such as:

  • QVT Operational Development Tools

  • QVT Operational SDK

  • QVT Operational Tests

Click:

Next

docs.title: Step 5 – Accept the Licence
docs.text:
Select:

I accept the terms of the license agreement

Click:

Finish

docs.title: Step 6 – Restart Eclipse
docs.text:
After installation, Eclipse will ask you to restart.

Click:

Restart Now

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
After restarting Eclipse, verify that QVTo was installed correctly:

  • Right-click a .qvto file
  • Select:
Run As → QVT Operational Transformation

If this option appears, QVTo is installed successfully.

docs.title: Alternative – Install from Downloaded Archive
docs.text:
If the direct update-site method does not work, you can still install QVTo from the archive manually.

Go to the official release page:

https://download.eclipse.org/mmt/qvto/builds/release/latest/index.html

Download the .zip file, for example:

QVTo-Updates-3.11.2.zip

Then in Eclipse:

Help → Install New Software... → Add... → Archive...

Select the downloaded .zip file and continue with the same steps:

Next → Next → Accept License → Finish

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Final tested version: QVTo 3.11.2

  • QVTo is still actively maintained, so newer versions may exist

  • Some Eclipse distributions already include QVTo

  • Use the direct update-site method first

  • Use the archive method only if the update-site method fails

docs.title: QVT Setup (Eclipse)
docs.text:
This guide is for setting up the QVT transformation engine in Eclipse. It is not required to run the MiSAR parser or generate PSM files, but it is necessary for transforming PSM to PIM.

The QVT transformation engine is used to transform the generated PSM into a PIM, which is the recovered architectural model of the microservice system.

docs.title: Install Eclipse Modeling Tools
docs.text: Download Eclipse Modeling Tools package. Latest version can be found at: https://www.eclipse.org/downloads/packages/

docs.title: Import Project
docs.text:
File → Open Projects from File System

Select the TransformationEngineNecessities folder located in the MiSAR project directory: MiSAR-Parser-and-Model-Transformation/TransformationEngineNecessities/

docs.title: Configure Metamodels
docs.text:
In case you cannot find the QVT Settings in the project properties, make sure you have installed the QVT Operational component as described in the manual installation guide.

Go to: Project → Properties → QVT Settings → Metamodel Mappings

Add:

docs.title: PIM
docs.text: Source Target http://localhost/mdd/PIM.ecore platform:/resource/.../PIM.ecore

docs.title: PSM
docs.text: Source Target http://localhost/mdd/PSM.ecore platform:/resource/.../PSM.ecore

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
In some Eclipse installations, QVTo may already be included.

If QVT Operational is not available in your Eclipse environment, please follow the manual installation steps described in this guide.
